title: Assign Deliveries to Vehicles Efficiently
real_world_story: A depot has a list of deliveries, each with an associated travel distance from the depot, and a set of vehicles of equal capacity. The dispatcher wants to assign deliveries to vehicles so that every vehicle carries a balanced workload. A greedy approach sorts the deliveries and distributes them among vehicles to reduce total route length.

real_world_connection.output_represents: Minimum possible maximum workload per vehicle
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Using a greedy ordering to balance assignments

problem_statement: Given N delivery jobs with workload values (such as travel distance) and K vehicles, partition the deliveries into K groups by assigning each delivery to a vehicle so that the maximum total workload assigned to any vehicle is as small as possible. Print the minimum possible maximum workload.
task: Find the smallest possible maximum workload across all vehicles using a greedy assignment.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and K, where N is the number of deliveries and K is the number of vehicles. The second line contains N integers representing the workload of each delivery.
output_format: Print the minimum possible maximum workload assigned to any vehicle.

examples.explanation: The workloads sum to 2600. One balanced assignment puts 900 alone on one vehicle, 700 + 200 on another, and 500 + 300 on the third, giving a maximum workload of 900.

expected_algorithm.name: Greedy
expected_algorithm.reason: A greedy approach that distributes workloads among vehicles can balance the maximum load reasonably while being simple and efficient.

hint: Think about how ordering the workloads helps distribute them.
Fill each vehicle up to the current target load.
Count how many vehicles a given target requires to determine feasibility.
real_world_takeaway: A greedy assignment keeps delivery workloads balanced across a fleet, which reduces idle time and helps every vehicle finish on time.
